summary: The note argues that parental and community involvement is central to student success and surveys examples of it in practice across several schools in 2023-2024. Examples include a parent engagement initiative, a business partnership, expanded school governance, cultural inclusion workshops, digital outreach, volunteer programs, and advocacy that helped pass the Community Education Reform Bill. The note ends with an empty section on partnerships.
one_line: Examples of parent, volunteer, business, and community engagement in schools and how they improve student outcomes, governance, inclusion, and advocacy.
key_facts: Lincoln Elementary School in Springfield unveiled 'Project Family Connect' on September 4, 2023, an initiative to involve parents in their children's education, spearheaded by principal Deborah Richards.

Research cited in the note says engaged parents can raise school performance, boost teacher morale, and improve student outcomes, including better behavior and higher likelihood of continuing education beyond high school.
The Tech for Tomorrow program launched on October 15, 2023, as a partnership between Greenwood High School and the local tech company SynerTech.
SynerTech provides cutting-edge equipment and professionals who mentor students in the Tech for Tomorrow program.
Rochester Middle School expanded its School Advisory Council in February 2024 so that parents and community representatives make up at least half of its members.
John Peterson (parent and local entrepreneur) and Maria Gonzalez (parent and social worker) actively participate in Rochester Middle School's School Advisory Council.

Assistant Principal David Nguyen introduced the Cultural Connection Workshops at Hampton Elementary School on January 27, 2024, bringing parents from various backgrounds together to discuss cultural values, traditions, and educational expectations.

Summit High School outreach coordinator Lisa Martin launched a communication strategy using social media, a mobile school app, and regular community webinars, as revealed at a conference on September 23, 2023.
The communication strategy helped working parents such as James and Emily Richardson, who struggled to participate because of irregular work hours, stay informed.

Oaks Middle School's volunteer program began in fall 2023, with volunteers including retired teacher Margaret Fisher and college student Alex Hernandez serving as reading mentors, homework helpers, and coaches.

The Community Education Reform Bill passed on August 30, 2023, emphasizing the role of communities in supporting education, after advocacy by a coalition of educators, parents, students, and community leaders.
Stephanie Clarke, a local librarian and parent, advocated in ways that opened new funding avenues for education-driven community projects.
